entries.title: Predecessor rule: 1991 Act Section 10 already required unanimity or majority
entries.summary: Before 2024, Section 10 of the 1991 Act, inserted with effect from 1 October 1993, provided that the Commission allocate business only by unanimous decision, transact business unanimously as far as possible, and otherwise decide by majority. The 1991 Act also fixed a six-year term and pay equal to a Supreme Court judge, but was silent on how commissioners were chosen.

entries.title: Supreme Court questions 'lightning speed' of Goel's appointment
entries.summary: After perusing the original file, the Constitution Bench asked the Attorney General why the process was completed within 24 hours, why the vacancy open since May was filled in a day, and why none of the four empanelled officers could serve the six-year term. The bench said it was examining the process, not Goel's credentials, and reserved judgment the same day.

sources.quote: Same day process, same day clearance, same day application, same day acceptance

entries.notes: The bench had asked for the file on 23 November 2022. The written judgment of 2 March 2023 (paras 187-195) sets out the same concerns in the Court's own words.

Venkataramani told the bench there was nothing disquieting about the appointment, that a selection mechanism and criteria existed, and that panels are drawn from a database of Secretary-rank officers. In the judgment the Court recorded his submission that there is a 'dearth' of officers who could serve a full six-year term.

entries.title: Supreme Court: PM, LoP and CJI to select CEC and ECs until Parliament legislates
entries.summary: A unanimous five-judge bench held that, until Parliament makes a law under Article 324(2), the President shall appoint the CEC and ECs on the advice of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party) and the Chief Justice of India. Justice Rastogi's concurring opinion added that ECs should have the same removal protection as the CEC. The Court appealed to Parliament to give the Commission an independent secretariat funded from the Consolidated Fund.

details.bench: K.M. Joseph (author), Ajay Rastogi (concurring), Aniruddha Bose, Hrishikesh Roy, C.T. Ravikumar
details.operative_direction: Para 239(I): committee of PM, LoP (or leader of largest opposition party) and CJI; holds good till Parliament legislates.
details.rastogi_directions: Para 126: same committee; desirable that ECs be removable only like a Supreme Court judge; ECs' service conditions not to be varied to their disadvantage.
details.secretariat: Para 239(II): 'fervent appeal' for a permanent secretariat and expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund.

entries.title: Arun Goel resigns, leaving CEC Rajiv Kumar as sole commissioner
entries.summary: Election Commissioner Arun Goel resigned and the President accepted it with effect from 9 March 2024, under Section 11(1) of the 2023 Act. With Pandey's post also vacant, CEC Rajiv Kumar was the only member days before the Lok Sabha election schedule was announced. Goel's term would have run to December 2027. The same day, the government issued a revised note moving the selection meeting from 15 to 14 March to fill both posts.
